in_text_mentions: Doppler ultrasound revealed bilateral stenosis, with 95% obstruction on the right and 70% on the left. An abdominal and pelvic CT scan documented the following findings: “Atherosclerotic disease of the abdominal aortic wall at the origin of the renal arteries, with apparent involvement of the ostium of the right renal artery, as well as ipsilateral renal atrophy, suggesting a renovascular etiology” (Figures 1, 2).

panels.rationale: Single-panel catheter angiogram of the right renal artery in a human patient, with a red arrow marking a focal stenosis near the aortic origin; the caption and in-text description (70% right renal artery stenosis causing recurrent flash pulmonary edema and resistant hypertension) directly support atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis. No skin, age or ethnicity information is provided. [raw subtype: atherosclerotic_renal_artery_stenosis]

in_text_mentions: lood pressure (BP) of 220/91 mmHg accompanied by signs of fluid overload. Lab studies were within normal limits. She was discharged after being treated with diuretics and anti-hypertensives. She presented again within a month with similar symptoms and BP of 188/79 mmHg. Due to recurrent flash pulmonary edema and resistant hypertension, a renal artery ultrasound was performed, which demonstrated atrophic right kidney and poorly visualized renal arteries. A subsequent renal angiogram showed 70% stenosis of the right renal artery, which was later intervened with a bare-metal stent (Figures 1, 2).
